question:
I am handing over a finished system to a client whose in-house team will keep developing it after delivery. Besides the program itself, what written material should I prepare for the client, for its end users and for my own organization, and for how long should it be retained?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
[JEV filter] kept 11 of 11 guidelines (JEV 'lenient' score > 0.5)

# Guidelines
- Prepare design work products that capture: (1) aspects of the problems solved using domain vocabulary, (2) the solution vocabulary, (3) the major decisions [SWEBOK excerpt be4b1e38f666b798e7d9] — these support the in-house team that will continue development after handover. (source: root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Software Design Documentation and Communication Methods/Recording Software Designs.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Record the design rationale — [SWEBOK excerpt 3632f2289fc30a05af8b] analysed — because reasons obvious to the original team will [SWEBOK excerpt b9822ef6022f81ed850e]. Continue capturing rationale for changes made during maintenance to sustain the software's long-term viability. (source: root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Produce a controlled transition package — a coordinated sequence of activities and accompanying documentation — to transfer the software progressively from the developer to the client's operations and maintenance team. (source: root/Software Maintenance Costs, Metrics, and Quality/Software Maintenance Processes and Activities.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Include program-understanding documentation (what the software does and how its parts work together) so the receiving team can support and modify it without needing to reverse-engineer the system from scratch. (source: root/Software Maintenance Costs, Metrics, and Quality/Software Maintenance Processes and Activities.md) [JEV 0.85]
- Prepare end-user-facing support material and establish a maintenance help-desk function, since the help desk is the end-user support channel that triggers assessment, prioritisation, and costing of maintenance requests and incidents. (source: root/Software Maintenance Costs, Metrics, and Quality/Software Maintenance Processes and Activities.md) [JEV 0.91]
- Develop and hand over a Software Configuration Management Plan (SCMP) — a living document covering: introduction (purpose, scope, terms), SCM management (organisation, responsibilities, authorities, applicable policies and procedures), SCM activities, SCM schedules, SCM resources, and provisions for SCMP maintenance. Keep it updated and approved throughout the software life cycle. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Plan Development.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Develop a maintenance plan — beginning at the decision to build the system — covering: scope of software maintenance, adaptation of maintenance processes and tools, and identification of the maintenance organisation. Precede it with a concept document that addresses quality objectives. (source: root/Software Maintenance Planning and Supporting Activities.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Document and hand over all [SWEBOK excerpt 03ad80de9ff11706d6a7] software/hardware licences and contracts, because these contractual agreements [SWEBOK excerpt a85f62e46bec9af8770c] that the client's team will need to manage. (source: root/Software Maintenance Planning and Supporting Activities.md) [JEV 0.91]
- Plan for ongoing documentation as a supporting maintenance activity: the maintainers should continue to produce documentation, perform SCM, verification and validation, problem resolution, SQA, reviews, vulnerability assessments, and audits throughout the maintenance phase. (source: root/Software Maintenance Planning and Supporting Activities.md) [JEV 0.94]
- Retain documentation for the full maintenance lifetime of the software: the maintenance phase [SWEBOK excerpt e5aabbce3fff8efbd15d], so documentation needed to understand, modify, or support the system should be kept at least that long. (source: root/Software Maintenance Planning and Supporting Activities.md) [JEV 0.71]
- Include release/version planning documentation — covering availability dates of individual requests, agreed content of subsequent releases, identified conflicts and alternatives, risk assessments, and back-out plans — to enable the client's team to manage future evolution safely. (source: root/Software Maintenance Planning and Supporting Activities.md) [JEV 0.97]
